CHAPTER FOUR

DATA PRESENTATION, ANALYSIS AND DISCUSSION OF FINDINGS

Study: Illustrative questionnaire results

Researcher review required: DRAFT FOR RESEARCHER REVIEW: Check every input count, objective assignment, reverse-coding instruction, question wording and source label against the original records. No hypothesis test or empirical citation has been generated.

4.1 Introduction

This chapter presents descriptive statistics derived solely from the frequency counts supplied for individual questionnaire items. Frequency tables show original response labels, and the numerical mean and standard deviation use the questionnaire coding and any specified reverse-scoring.

4.2 Survey Coverage and Analytical Basis

No overall sample size was declared. These figures are metadata only: valid N is calculated separately as the sum of supplied frequency counts for each item. No questionnaire return rate can be calculated from these inputs.

Sample SD divides by N−1 (Bessel correction), treating observed frequencies as a sample. For N=1, sample SD is undefined.

4.4 Discussion of Descriptive Findings

Objective 1: Describe responses to Item 5

For Item 5, 153 valid category responses were provided. The most frequent response was Agree (45; 29.41%). The frequency-weighted mean was 3.21; the sample standard deviation was 1.45. The scored median was 4.00, and the scored mode was 4. These results describe the item distribution; they do not establish a causal explanation or statistical significance.

4.5 Limitations of Frequency-Only Analysis

The supplied figures are marginal frequency distributions for individual questionnaire items. They do not identify how any respondent answered other items. Therefore correlations, regressions, group comparisons (t-tests or ANOVA), Cronbach's alpha, factor analysis, respondent-level composite scores, and hypothesis significance cannot be computed from this input alone. Neither sample-size nor population-size metadata reconstruct paired observations. Treat numeric Likert means/SD as summaries based on an approximately equally spaced coding convention; the underlying response categories are ordinal.

This draft deliberately contains no invented respondent-level records, response rates, hypothesis-test results, p-values, literature citations or causal claims.
